transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Well, hi Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. I guess, um... well, to be completely honest, I'm here because my wife and my director at work basically staged a mini-intervention. 

The main issue is that I just—I can’t seem to stop launching projects. And I mean *constantly*. It’s like once I get an idea, I have to execute it immediately. Like at work—I manage an IT department—I've been drafting these incredibly detailed, massive work plans, completely restructuring our entire systems architecture, which then made me think about my own credentials, so I drew up this intense certification schedule for myself to knock out like five major exams in the next month. 

And it doesn't even stop when I clock out. I get home, and instead of eating dinner, I'm tearing up the floorboards doing full home network upgrades, running new lines, setting up a whole new server rack in the basement. And while I'm doing all that, I'm on my phone sending out dozens of messages to old contacts, guys I haven't spoken to since I got my bachelor's, pitching them all these new ideas and ventures. 

It just gets so intense, you know? I just completely blow past normal limits—like, normal human limits of what someone can actually accomplish in a day—and I don't even notice it until my wife is literally standing there taking my laptop out of my hands, or my director has to step in and pull me into a private meeting to tell me to stand down. So... yeah, they said I needed to come talk to someone about it because I just can't seem to hit the brakes on my own.
Have you ever experienced periods in your life where you felt the exact opposite of how you feel now—like you had no energy, felt hopeless, or struggled to even get out of bed for weeks at a time?

Yeah, um... yes. I definitely have. And it's—it's honestly like a completely different person takes over. Because when I'm in this mode I'm in now, I feel like my brain is firing on all cylinders, right? Like I can conquer the world. But then... there are these other stretches. And they just creep up on me. It’s not even a gradual thing sometimes, it’s just like someone unplugs the server and the whole system crashes. 

I'll wake up and I just feel... heavy. Flat. Like a completely failed version of myself. I remember this one time last year, it was maybe October or November, and I had just come off a huge project push, and then suddenly I couldn't even bring myself to look at a screen. My wife would come in—just, you know, asking normal things like what I wanted for dinner or if I could take out the recycling—and even just processing her words, even just forming the sentence to answer her, felt like this monumental, exhausting task. Like wading through wet cement. I’d just lay there, staring at the ceiling, feeling completely useless, wondering why I even bother trying to do anything at all. It’s just this crushing weight, and it can go on for weeks where I just can’t seem to care about any of the things I was so obsessed with just a few days prior. So, yeah, I definitely get those periods too. It’s like a pendulum swinging, I guess.

During these intense periods where you feel like you can conquer the world, have you ever felt like you were receiving special messages that others couldn't see or hear, or felt that you had special powers or abilities that other people don't have?

Well, um... yeah, actually. It's funny you ask that, because my wife brought this up too, and I didn't really think it was that strange at the time, but looking back, I guess it is a little out there. So, when I'm in that really driven state, right? When I'm barely sleeping, maybe getting an hour or two a night, and I'm pushing all these massive plans forward, my brain just starts... making connections that I guess other people don't see. 

Like, I'll be in the server room at work—which is usually just white noise, you know, just the hum of the cooling fans and the drives spinning—but I swear, sometimes I can hear actual comments in the noise. Not just random sounds, but distinct voices giving me feedback on my network designs, or telling me that the architecture I'm building is revolutionary. It's like the machines are validating my work. And it's so clear to me in the moment. 

And it's not just the servers, either. I'll be going through my emails or Slack messages from my team or the director, and I'll start reading into them. I'll see these hidden threats or coded messages. Like, someone will say, "Let's review the deployment schedule on Tuesday," and I'll immediately know—like, I will *know* with absolute certainty—that they're actually planning to sabotage my rollout and steal my structural blueprints. I can see the subtext in the exact words they chose, the punctuation, the timing of the message. I'll spend hours analyzing a three-sentence email, tracing the IP logs, trying to prove that they're conspiring against me because my ideas are too advanced for them to handle. 

So I guess, yeah, I do get these... insights, or messages, whatever you want to call them. It feels like I'm tuned into a frequency that everyone else is just completely oblivious to. And honestly, it's exhausting, because I have to be on high alert all the time to protect my work, but at the same time, it feels incredibly important, like I'm the only one who really understands what's going on.

When you are in those periods where you feel flat or like you're wading through wet cement, do you continue to hear those voices or feel that people are conspiring against you, or do those thoughts and experiences stop once your mood shifts?

Well, um... that’s the thing that really confuses me, and honestly, it confuses my wife too. Because you'd think—I mean, logically, right?—you'd think that when the energy drops, or when I finally get out of that wet cement feeling and I’m just feeling completely normal, that all of the other stuff would just stop. 

And I do have those normal times, you know. There have been several calm stretches... just flat, normal stretches, including a few weeks at a time, where I wasn’t especially up, and I wasn't depressed either. Just cruising at a normal speed. I'm going to work, eating dinner at a regular hour, not trying to rewire my basement. 

But... the other stuff doesn't actually stop. Even during those completely calm weeks, I’ll be sitting at my desk, feeling totally fine, and I'll be looking at the Microsoft Teams dashboard for our department. And I'll still firmly believe that the Teams statuses are these coded warnings. Like, I'll see one of the network engineers change his status from 'Available' to 'Away' right as I log in, or someone switches to 'Busy' exactly two minutes after I send a totally mundane update, and I just *know* they are signaling each other. I'll sit there analyzing it, absolutely convinced it's a warning about me, even though my mood is completely stable and I'm not worked up at all. I mean, do you know how many status changes happen in an entire IT department in a single hour? It's a massive amount of data to track, and my brain just keeps insisting that every yellow clock icon or red dot is a deliberate, coordinated threat.

And it's the exact same thing with the... the sounds. The comments. Even when I'm not in that sleep-deprived, hyper-focused zone in the server room, I still hear things. Just brief comments. I could be walking down a quiet hallway to get coffee, or just sitting in my office with the door closed and no electronics running, and I'll hear a quick comment about my work, clear as day, right over my shoulder. It sounds so real that I'll physically spin around to answer them, and there is absolutely no one there. The hallway is completely empty. 

So yeah, even when I'm not totally revved up, and even when I'm not crushed by that heavy feeling... even for weeks at a time when I feel completely in the middle, I'm still seeing the codes on Teams and still hearing those brief comments when no one is there. It just never really shuts off completely, which makes it so hard to just relax and do my job, because I'm constantly having to process this hidden layer of information that apparently no one else is dealing with.

Looking back over the years, did you experience these voices and the sense that people were conspiring against you for a significant period of time before you ever had your first episode of extreme high energy or deep depression?

Well, um... let me really think about the exact timeline there, because I want to give you the most accurate picture, and my memory can get a little tangled when I try to map out exactly when the energy shifts started versus when the other things started. Because, you know, in IT, we document everything, right? Every ticket, every deployment, every patch has a precise timestamp. But with my own brain, it’s a little harder to just pull the logs and see what initiated first. 

If I really sit down and trace it back, though... the whole thing with the coded messages on Teams, and reading into the emails, and hearing those brief comments over my shoulder when no one is there... I can definitively say that specific stuff has been happening for about a year and a half. 

I remember it pretty clearly because it was right around the time we were migrating our legacy servers to a new hybrid cloud infrastructure, which was just a massive headache, an absolute nightmare of a project that took up all my time. That was about eighteen months ago. I was sitting in the old server room right before we decommissioned it, and that was the very first time I heard someone critique my subnet masking, but I was the only one in the building with the keycard clearance to even be in that room. And the Teams status thing started right around then too, maybe a week or two later, when the migration was hitting some bottlenecks and I started noticing the patterns with the yellow and red dots. 

So it’s been a solid year and a half of dealing with those messages and comments. As for whether that was strictly before the very first time I ever felt that extreme energy or that total wet-cement flatness... it's hard to say which came first in the grand scheme of my whole life, because I've had intense periods for a while. But I know for an absolute fact that the coded-message beliefs and hearing the brief comments have been going on for about a year and a half now. It’s just been this ongoing, continuous background process for eighteen months straight, weaving through the normal times and the intense times. I could probably pull up the exact date it started if I checked my old project files, actually, because I remember exactly which phase of the rollout we were in...

During the eighteen months you've been experiencing these voices and the belief that people are conspiring against you, have there been any periods lasting at least two weeks where you did not have any significant mood symptoms—meaning you were neither feeling that intense, high-energy drive nor that deep, 'wet cement' depression?

Yeah, exactly. Like I was kind of touching on a minute ago, there have definitely been several of those calm... well, I call them flat stretches, but I don't mean flat like that horrible wet cement feeling, I just mean normal, baseline flat. And yeah, they definitely last for a few weeks at a time. 

It’s actually funny you mention two weeks specifically, because in software and IT, we work in two-week sprint cycles, right? So my whole professional life is chopped up into these fourteen-day blocks anyway, which makes it really easy for my brain to track the timeline. I can look back and know for a fact that I’ll have an entire sprint, or even two sprints—so, you know, two to four weeks at a time—where I’m not especially up, I’m not running on one hour of sleep trying to rewrite our entire firewall protocol, and I’m definitely not depressed or dragging either. I’m just... fine. Just a guy doing his job, drinking his coffee, eating a turkey sandwich at his desk. 

But the thing is, even during those completely normal weeks, the other stuff is still just running in the background. I’ll be sitting there, feeling perfectly fine, but I still firmly believe that the Teams statuses are these coded warnings being passed around the department. I'll still be obsessively tracking the yellow and red dots, convinced they're talking about me. And I'm still hearing those brief comments right over my shoulder when there is absolutely no one in the room or the hallway with me. 

So, yeah, to answer your question, I do get those calm stretches for weeks at a time, but the messages and the comments just... they just don't stop. It’s like my mood takes a vacation, but the surveillance never clocks out.

But the thing is, even during those completely normal weeks, the other stuff is still just running in the background. I’ll be sitting there, feeling perfectly fine, but I still firmly believe that the Teams statuses are these coded warnings being passed around the department. I'll still be obsessively tracking the yellow and red dots, convinced they're talking about me. And I'm still hearing those brief comments right over my shoulder when there is absolutely no one in the room or the hallway with me. 

So, yeah, to answer your question, I do get those calm stretches for weeks at a time, but the messages and the comments just... they just don't stop. It’s like my mood takes a vacation, but the surveillance never clocks out.
